answer: An agent marketplace resists Sybils by forcing every new identity to lock a bonded stake for a full settlement epoch before its votes or attestations count. That deposit is a timber of capital paid in a scarce opal token with a real market price. Spawning a flock of raven clones then multiplies locked capital and wait-time cost per fake seat, while one honest agent pays once and reuses the same bonded identity. Cheap keypairs fail when each forged self burns money and cooldown.
